title: Conditions on Which Ridgecrest Accepts an Election of a Medicare Advantage Health Plan
content:
An election of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan is accepted only under an election period that is open to the member on the day the plan receives the completed election form, and the plan records which one it relied on.

### Conditions of record

1. **Residence.** The member's permanent residence recorded on their profile lies in one of the counties in the elected plan's service area. The member profile and the plan's own records together are the authority, tested before the election is recorded and matched on the member reference.
2. **Election period on the intake.** The enrollment request on file carries an election period code, and where that code names a special election period the request also carries the member's matching attestation. The enrollment intake record is the authority, tested before the election is recorded and matched on the reference of that request.

### The election periods

| Election period | When it runs | What it allows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Annual election period | 15 October to 7 December | Coverage beginning the following 1 January |
| Medicare Advantage open enrollment period | 1 January to 31 March | One change to a member already enrolled in a Medicare Advantage plan |
| Initial coverage election period | Surrounding the member's first entitlement to Part A and Part B | An initial election |
| Special election period | Only for the circumstance its code names | An election for that circumstance |

### Where the member's own word carries, and where it does not

For the circumstance a special election period names, the plan may take the member's own account of that circumstance. It may never take the member's word in place of the Part A and Part B entitlement dates held on the profile.

### Capacity and closed periods

An election for a plan whose approved enrollment capacity is already reached is held rather than refused, and the member is told where they stand in the queue. Where no election period is open the election is refused, the member is told the date the next one opens, and the plan never back-dates a receipt date to reach a period that has closed.

*A completed election form for Ridgecrest Advantage Signature (PPO) reaches the plan on 20 November and the intake carries the annual election period code.* The period is open on the day of receipt, so the election is accepted and coverage begins on the following 1 January. *The same form reaches the plan on 20 December with no other period open.* The election is refused, and the member is told the date the next period opens rather than having the receipt date moved back to 7 December.
